Definitions, widths, alignment and padding of the atomic counter types and their counter fields.

findings.text: Single-copy accessors expose reading and writing of the atomic counter field as one load or store with single-evaluation semantics, usable for plain observation and initialization without stronger ordering.

The 32-bit surface advertises value-returning add and subtract plus old-value-fetching add, subtract, bitwise and, clear-bits, or and xor, each in default, relaxed, acquire and release orderings, together with a void clear-bits updater.

The 64-bit surface aliases its initializer, reader and writer to the 32-bit forms and advertises the same arithmetic and bitwise returning and fetching families in all four orderings, plus void clear-bits and a conditional decrement acting only on positive values.

The exclusive-access backend supplies void updaters, new-value-returning arithmetic and old-value-fetching arithmetic and bitwise operations for both 32-bit and 64-bit counters, plus a 64-bit conditional decrement and narrow plus wide compare-exchange helpers including a 128-bit form.

The single-instruction extension backend supplies store-only updaters, old-value-fetching primitives and derived new-value-returning arithmetic for both widths, plus conditional 64-bit decrement and single-instruction compare-exchange helpers.

Ordering suffixes map to hardware ordering controls: the default form combines a full inner-shareable barrier with release-store behaviour, relaxed carries no barrier or acquire plus release annotation, acquire uses acquire-load behaviour, and release uses release-store behaviour, with compiler memory effects except for relaxed.

Void forms only update the counter, fetch forms return the value seen before the update, arithmetic return forms return the value after the update, subtract is defined through negated add and bitwise and through complemented clear-bits in the extension backend, conditional decrement leaves negative inputs unchanged and otherwise decrements once, and compare-exchange returns the value observed at the address.
Each backend header defines a once-only inclusion marker, and the exclusive-access header additionally defines an empty single-letter marker used as a placeholder in its generic operation templates.

A 128-bit helper type overlays one wide value with a pair of low and high 64-bit halves in declaration order, allowing wide compare-exchange to move the halves through separate registers while returning a single wide value.

Exclusive updates behave as attempt until success with reservation loss causing retry, compare-exchange exiting early on mismatch without storing, extension compare loops retrying while the observed value changes, and conditional decrement aborting without storing on negative input.

No software spinlock or blocking primitive is acquired; atomicity comes from hardware reservation monitoring or single-copy atomic instructions, with ordering enforced by barrier and acquire plus release annotations rather than mutual-exclusion state.

Reservation-based loops can retry indefinitely under contention or reservation loss, sub-word compare-exchange must ignore upper register bits when comparing, some bitwise immediates lack dedicated encoding support and use registers, and the routed 32-bit extension subtract-return helper reuses the default-ordering fetch instead of propagating its suffix unlike its 64-bit counterpart.
The stable entry surface in these fragments is the arch_atomic and arch_atomic64 family covering plain access, ordered arithmetic and bitwise updates, and conditional decrement.
A helper owned by another dossier is referenced for constraint handling and is not specified here.
